use_case_name: Add Files to an Existing Archive

claims.content: Allow the user to add one or more files or archives to an already existing archive without destroying the existing content.

goal.raw_text: Allow the user to add one or more files or archives to an already existing archive without destroying the existing content.

claims.content: User

The user selects one or more files or archives from the file manager interface and initiates the add operation by pressing the 'Add' button on the toolbar, selecting 'Add' from a context menu, or using an equivalent system command.

trigger.raw_text: The user selects one or more files or archives from the file manager interface and initiates the add operation by pressing the 'Add' button on the toolbar, selecting 'Add' from a context menu, or using an equivalent system command.

claims.content: The user selects one or more files or archives from the file manager interface.
The user initiates the add operation by pressing the 'Add' button on the toolbar, selecting 'Add' from a context menu, or using an equivalent system command.
The system opens the Create archive Interface (also used for updating archives), where the user can confirm or adjust settings such as compression format, output location, and encryption.
The user confirms the operation by clicking 'OK' or pressing Ctrl+Alt+Enter to add the selected files to the existing archive without destroying its current content.
Alternatively, the user can add files to the archive layout using keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+A to add files or Ctrl+F to add a folder, instead of using the toolbar or context menu.
Alternatively, during the update process, the user may choose to encrypt the archive by setting a password and optionally a keyfile before confirming the operation.
The name of the compressed file being updated remains the same as it was before the update.
The storage space of the compressed file remains the same as it was before the update.
The objects contained in the created archive are not destroyed, deleted, or left empty.
Existing objects retain their content and name and remain saved at the same space of the computer system where they were initially stored.
Encryption (lock) can be applied to the archive by setting a password and optionally a keyfile.
